chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: Nights of listening in Kansas City: Pete Johnson and Joe Turner
summary: When he first arrived he went to every club after work, hearing Bus Moten and Pete Johnson's steady beat behind Joe Turner on 12th Street.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, you'd wanted to have a big band ever since you heard that guy, hadn't you?

You know, evidently that was the thing I think that really turned me around, when I heard all them trumpets, you know, and heard the saxaphone and trombones over here doing something else. That was it, you know.

All of that. And then, not to speak of like when I first came to Kansas City, when I first came to Kansas City, I would go somewhere every night and listen because I would get off about 1:30 at night, and during that time, the joints was going until six, seven, eight, 9:00 in the morning, but the place I was working for, I got off at 1:30. So this give me a chance to make all the clubs, you know, and I used to come into clubs and I'd enjoy coming up and listening to Bus Moten's group, leave there and go hear another group, leave there and go hear another group, then go down on 12th Street and hear Pete Johnson play the blues and Joe Turner sing the blues. And Pete sitting there (tapping table) just for 20, 30 or 40 minutes, and just keeping a steady thing, steady roll,
steady rock and roll, steady beat. And Joe singing for 30 minutes. Well, I'd never seen anything like that in my life.

You know, it was exciting. It was exciting and -- it was exciting because I liked it, you know? You hear something you like and so I just never could get enough of it. I never wanted to go to sleep at night because I was afraid I would miss something, yeah.
